chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Muthanna, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A parchment was found in the sheath of the sword of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): 'Verily, the most transgressive of people toward God, Mighty and Majestic, is the killer who kills other than the one who was trying to kill him, and the one who strikes someone other than the one who struck him. And whoever claims lineage other than his (biological) father, then he is a disbeliever in what God revealed to Muhammad. And whoever initiates a criminal act, or shelters one who initiated a criminal act — God, Mighty and Majestic, will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection, any ransom nor any substitute.'

key_terms.أَعْتَى: Most transgressive/insolent — the superlative of 'utuww (haughtiness, defiance of God), indicating the highest degree of rebellion
key_terms.صَحِيفَة: A written parchment or scroll — in early Islamic usage, an official document with legal or prophetic authority
key_terms.صَرْف: Ransom or redemptive exchange — in eschatological context, any means of buying oneself out of divine punishment
key_terms.عَدْل: A substitute or equivalent — any alternate compensation offered on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.قَائِمُ السَّيْفِ: The hilt or sheath of the sword — a place where important documents were sometimes stored for safekeeping

ai.seo_question: What three sins make a person the most transgressive toward God according to a document found in the Prophet's sword?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits the contents of a written parchment discovered in the hilt/sheath of the Prophet Muhammad's sword, citing three grave offenses that make a person among the most transgressive toward God. The three offenses are: retaliatory killing of the wrong person (killing someone other than one's actual aggressor), striking the wrong person in revenge, and disowning one's biological father by falsely claiming another lineage. Additionally, those who commit criminal acts or harbor criminals will face no mercy on the Day of Judgment. The document's presence in the Prophet's sword underscores its authoritative and legal nature, as swords were symbols of rule and justice in early Islamic society.
word_analysis: his killer/the one trying to kill him
